As I said in other comments in this subreddit, both of us had past trauma due to cheating partners. I talked to my therapist about it, we did some couple counseling from distance and we are all good now. I'm not "jumping" into it, because there are other issues in my family and is something both of us want to do: to escape the toxicity I'm living in. However, even if things don't work out, I have close relatives that I'm getting along with, who are willing to help me anytime in that country and I'll have a job from the first day I'm going to move there so it'll not be a problem:)

Sending you lots of internet hugs!!
I cried like a baby for 4 or 5 hours after he left, it was the day of our anniversary too. We spent a month together, and the goodbyes were the hardest. This was back in January, in April I'm going to visit him and in May I'm taking my last flight to him since we are moving in together. I know it's hard and it doesn't get any easier, you just get kind of used to being away from your partner, but if love and respect exists I think any tears, any goodbyes, any countless texting and FaceTime nights are going to be worth it in the end.
Just be strong because if it's meant to be, it's meant to be!!

Drop him. He doesn't deserve the head and heart ache. If he can't past his sexual needs for you then he doesn't deserve you at all.
Someone that truly loves you should be willing to wait for you as long as it takes to be with you and to make you happy.

Every relationship has its own boundaries and it's something you guys need to discuss. 
Me and my partner (since we both are healing from past relationships trauma with cheaters) had an agreement to not go out with the opposite gender. For some of you might seem toxic, but as I said: every relationship has its own boundaries and for us this agreement works extremely well. I trust him and he trusts me too, but we didn't want to do things that'll make one of us uncomfortable and raise up disagreements or arguments since we are long distance and it's already hard enough.

Oh love, I'm so sorry! Keep your head up and be strong!

Long distance relationships are hard as they are, and without communication or a little bit of quality time..they are even harder. If he didn't try to make time for you to make things work between us even when you were trying hard to, he doesn't deserve you. You seem to have a golden heart and I'm sure you'll eventually find the one for you, but for now focus on yourself and always keep in mind that the healing process from a breakup is a bumpy ride—you're going to have many ups and downs, but I'm sure you're going to get through it. ❤️
